source.title: In-Context Language Learning: Architectures and Algorithms
source.authors: Ekin Akyürek; Bai-Lin Wang; Yoon Kim; Jacob Andreas

record.tranche_reason: The study uses attention visualization to examine induction-like head behavior in a synthetic in-context language-learning task, rather than reproducing the original method.
record.gate_note: The study directly describes a Transformer composing previous-token heads and a later head matching two-token contexts. Its probe results measure n-gram information in hidden states, and its inserted n-gram-head results measure deliberately added heads; neither directly tests naturally formed induction-head behavior, so they are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: In a new synthetic setting (in-context learning of regular languages), the study reports naturally formed previous-token heads composing with a later context-matching head in a trained Transformer. This bears on V1's mechanism, though the evidence is attention visualisation only.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that Transformers trained on regular ICLL develop n-gram heads (higher-order induction heads) and that their ICLL predictions resemble smoothed n-gram models. They also conclude that hard-wiring n-gram heads improves ICLL and natural language modelling. They acknowledge the visualisation does not show the heads actually compute n-gram statistics.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses synthetic regular-language ICLL and attention visualization of n-gram matching; it does not report an explicit replication of the original study's method.

fits_no_version.finding: Transformer next-token predictions are closest to smoothed n-gram models. The large Transformer's TVD is 0.16 to the learned reweighter and 0.21 to the 3-gram model; the 2-layer Transformer's TVD is 0.20 to the 2-gram vs 0.25 to the 3-gram model. Probes recover 2-gram and 3-gram statistics better from Transformers than from other architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context learning of formal languages in Transformers behaves like in-context n-gram estimation, with n growing with depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Hard-wired n-gram heads inserted into RetNet, GLA and Transformers improve ICLL TVD and accuracy (Table 1a). They also cut 340M-model perplexity on SlimPajama by up to 6.7% (Table 1b). These heads are built in on purpose, not naturally formed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fixed induction-style (n-gram) attention heads are a useful architectural prior for sequence models.

record.problems: The head evidence is an attention visualization of one stated model and an example sequence; the study does not report a causal ablation of the heads or a direct test of output copying.
record.rows_left_out: Section 5.2 and Figures 5 and 7 report probes of n-gram representations, not head-specific behavior. Table 1 reports results after n-gram heads are deliberately inserted, so those results do not establish natural formation.

untested.parts: Whether the context-matching head copies the attended token into the output; the exact first-order [A][B]…[A]→[B] pattern; attention-only models; any causal ablation of the heads.

missing.what: Statement that the layer 5 head does not selectively attend to tokens generated in the same DFA state. It qualifies what the matching head keys on.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. It could arguably bear on V4 (induction-like heads appearing in a new data setting), but this is one model and one example, so no V4 verdict is given. V3 is not tested: the models are small and the task is synthetic, and the behavioural n-gram similarity is not attributed to specific heads causally. There is no training-dynamics analysis (V2, V7) and no variation of data properties affecting head formation (V5).

versions.untested_parts: The study shows a higher-order, two-token context-matching pattern, but does not directly test output copying or the exact first-order [A][B] … [A] → [B] behavior.

rows.measure: Attention target for contexts matching the recent two-token context
rows.value: The layer 5 head attends to tokens in the C position following matching 2-grams; the example input ends in nh and the head attends to tokens in contexts nhX.
rows.note: The authors describe this as a higher-order analog of induction heads. The study reports the attention pattern, but does not directly test whether the attended-to token is copied into the output.
rows.check: State is correct. The head matches on a 2-token prefix rather than V1's 1-token [A][B]…[A] pattern; the Figure 4 caption says the match is 2-gram, not 1-gram. Output copying is not tested. The model has feed-forward layers, so it is not attention-only. Evidence is one example sequence (i=50:80) from one model.

source_check.correct: Higher-order context-matching attention is observed: layer 5 attends to C positions in ABC … AB sequences. For V1's full single-token match-and-copy mechanism, state=cannot_determine; output copying is untested, rather than demonstrated to be incomplete.

relation.reason: The study reports its own measurements of naturally formed previous-token and context-matching heads, in addition to experiments using hard-wired heads.

tranche.reason: Regular-language ICLL supplies a new setting with naturally learned higher-order induction-like attention patterns; this is not an explicit replication of the original method.

source_check.notes: The authors_conclusion paraphrase is accurate. The model includes feed-forward layers; the evidence concerns a higher-order analog, and the authors explicitly caution that attention visualisation does not establish computation of n-gram statistics.

statements.correction: §5.1 and Figure 4: 8-layer, 1-head Transformer; N=2500; previous-token heads in layers 2 and 3; two-token context-matching head in layer 5; structural evidence from attention visualisation.
statements.problem: The study is omitted from the prose despite R1 being listed as provenance; R1 alone records only the previous-token component.

statements.correction: Layers 2 and 3 attend to previous tokens; their composition supplies two-token context; layer 5 attends after matching two-token prefixes. Figure 4 illustrates one sequence. Canonical single-token output copying and causal necessity are untested.
statements.problem: The architecture, layers and matching pattern are correct, but higher-order matching does not establish a scope limitation of V1; missing ablation is an evidence limitation.
